statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks were judged across the exposed directory, its only linked page, and an HTTP failure state.

page.notes: A server-generated directory index linking to a six-byte diagnostic/status token. No other routes were discoverable; robots.txt and sitemap.xml return 404.

checkOutcomes.method: Screenshot under prefers-color-scheme: dark plus DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture: white canvas and black text; the DOM contains no CSS or color-scheme declaration.
The reduced-motion probe confirmed the emulated preference and found zero active animations; the page has no scripts or styles.
High-contrast emulation leaves the native heading/link legible, and Lighthouse reports no contrast failures.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM route inspection and source/CSS inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The only route change, from the directory to a.html, is a plain cross-document link with no CSS or view-transition styling, so it swaps abruptly.
Neither representative page has scroll-linked motion, parallax, scrollytelling, or reveal effects to implement.
checkOutcomes.reason: Neither representative page has scroll-linked motion, parallax, scrollytelling, or reveal effects to implement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither page exposes gesture-driven controls, carousels, swipe actions, or custom pointer interactions.
checkOutcomes.reason: Neither page exposes gesture-driven controls, carousels, swipe actions, or custom pointer interactions.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The pages have no navigation chrome and no meaningful scroll journey; the short static content does not warrant scroll-aware chrome.
checkOutcomes.reason: The pages have no navigation chrome and no meaningful scroll journey; the short static content does not warrant scroll-aware chrome.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip, menu, popover, or other anchored overlay exists on either page.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, menu, popover, or other anchored overlay exists on either page.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The link is labelled only “a.html”; its destination is an unheaded token with no navigation cue, context, focus cue, or return path.
Load screenshots and DOM show no popup, banner, interstitial, or overlay.
No overlay, disclosure, select, picker, or rich control is present, so no dismissible primitive is required.
checkOutcomes.reason: No overlay, disclosure, select, picker, or rich control is present, so no dismissible primitive is required.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The pages contain only their bare content and native browser styling, with no decorative or application chrome.
At a requested 360px viewport Chrome lays the page out at 980 CSS px and scales it to 0.367 because meta viewport is absent. This is a desktop canvas scaled down, not responsive reflow.
There are no reusable components or component containers; only an h1, list, link, and plain token are rendered.
checkOutcomes.reason: There are no reusable components or component containers; only an h1, list, link, and plain token are rendered.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The sole interactive element is a native anchor; Lighthouse target-size and link-name audits pass and browser-native keyboard focus remains available.
The first viewport says only “Index of /” and exposes a filename. It does not explain the AFIP-facing purpose, intended audience, or useful primary action.

checkOutcomes.method: End-to-end walkthrough of the only visible link
checkOutcomes.evidence: Following the only action reaches a page containing only the opaque token “fe010”, with no heading, explanation, next step, or return control.
A nonexistent route returns a generic Apache 404 with no home link, search, retry guidance, or recovery action.
Lighthouse measured LCP 0.8s, CLS 0, and TBT 0ms; trace measured LCP 1262ms and no blocking tasks.
Mobile layout observer and Lighthouse both measured CLS 0 with no layout-shift entries.

checkOutcomes.method: Trace, layout observer, and DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Trace and layout observers found zero long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; the page ships no JavaScript.
HAR records only two requests and 915 transferred bytes, with no render-blocking candidates; the only failed request is a tiny favicon and does not delay content.
DOM and HAR show no JavaScript, CSS, fonts, media, or third-party code, so there is no shipped unused or duplicate bundle.
The only interactive element is a native anchor with a discernible name; there are no forms, images, canvas, or custom controls. Lighthouse link-name passes.
Lighthouse color-contrast passes and screenshots show native black text/blue link on white with clear contrast.
The homepage has an h1 but no landmarks or language declaration, while a.html has no heading at all. The destination therefore lacks a meaningful document structure.
At desktop size the native heading and body text are unclipped and high contrast, with no custom fonts or mixed-font rendering problems.
Both pages omit meta viewport; a 360px device receives a 980px layout scaled to 36.7%, making native text much smaller than intended despite no horizontal overflow.
Lighthouse logs a 404 console/network error for /favicon.ico, which is also present in the HAR.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML, DOM compatibility-mode probe, and destination response inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The server emits an HTML 3.2 Final public doctype that Chrome treats as BackCompat/quirks mode; a.html is six bytes of text with no authored document structure.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices audits and DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse finds no BFCache blocker, deprecated permission prompt, paste prevention, source-map issue, or third-party-cookie problem; the page ships no script or input handlers.
The homepage title is the generic “Index of /” and has no meta description; a.html has neither title nor description.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM probe, mobile layout, robots fetch, and Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: The anchor is technically crawlable but its text is only “a.html”; neither page has a viewport meta element, and /robots.txt returns 404.

checkOutcomes.method: HTTP fetch and indexing metadata probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Pages return 200, but expose no canonical or hreflang signals; both robots.txt and sitemap.xml return 404, leaving no explicit crawl policy or inventory.
Neither page represents an article, product, organisation profile, event, place, or other rich entity; the exposed directory/token has no legitimate rich-result entity to encode.
checkOutcomes.reason: Neither page represents an article, product, organisation profile, event, place, or other rich entity; the exposed directory/token has no legitimate rich-result entity to encode.

checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and frame protection are absent. Both first-party cookies are set without Secure or HttpOnly and with SameSite=None.
Tracker and HAR evidence shows zero third-party origins, zero known trackers, only two requests, and no exposed client secret.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse permission audits and DOM flow inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse confirms no geolocation or notification request on load. No login, account, or authentication flow exists, so WebAuthn is not relevant here.
No HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors is configured.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML and no-JS discoverability comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Both pages are fully present in raw server responses and render without JavaScript; discoverability evidence confirms they are not JS shells.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM, HAR, and source response inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No runtime scripts, async dependencies, overlays, menus, background work, or mutable DOM state exist that could become fragile.
This is a tiny static server directory/diagnostic surface, not an app-like experience; a manifest, service worker, and installability are not proportionate requirements.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a tiny static server directory/diagnostic surface, not an app-like experience; a manifest, service worker, and installability are not proportionate requirements.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The tested 404 is a generic server page with no route back to the homepage or useful recovery action.
Neither page declares html[lang] (Lighthouse confirms the failure), so assistive technology and translation tooling cannot reliably identify the content language.
The representative pages display no dates, numbers, currency, duration, calendar, address, or other locale-sensitive value.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative pages display no dates, numbers, currency, duration, calendar, address, or other locale-sensitive value.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No date, event, schedule, timestamp, recurrence, or time-zone-dependent concept is exposed.
checkOutcomes.reason: No date, event, schedule, timestamp, recurrence, or time-zone-dependent concept is exposed.

checkOutcomes.evidence: There is no consent, upsell, subscription, advertising, destructive action, hidden offer, or deceptive choice; only one plain link is present.
No form or user input exists on the representative pages. Generic HTTP recovery is judged separately under core-task and resilience checks.
checkOutcomes.reason: No form or user input exists on the representative pages. Generic HTTP recovery is judged separately under core-task and resilience checks.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No input fields, sign-in, address, payment, or signup form exists.
checkOutcomes.reason: No input fields, sign-in, address, payment, or signup form exists.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No commercial, checkout, subscription, consent, authentication, or account-management flow exists.
checkOutcomes.reason: No commercial, checkout, subscription, consent, authentication, or account-management flow exists.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The image audit found zero images and HAR shows no fonts, media, or decorative assets; only 915 bytes transferred.
The page has no scripts or background requests; trace found no long tasks and HAR recorded only the document and failed favicon.
There are zero third-party origins and no scripts, fonts, image, video, audio, or animation payload.
This exposed surface is a bare directory/diagnostic token with no safe user capability or transactional form for an agent to invoke; adding WebMCP tooling would not be meaningful.
checkOutcomes.reason: This exposed surface is a bare directory/diagnostic token with no safe user capability or transactional form for an agent to invoke; adding WebMCP tooling would not be meaningful.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The surface performs no language, summarisation, classification, or other inference task where a built-in on-device model would improve the experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: The surface performs no language, summarisation, classification, or other inference task where a built-in on-device model would improve the experience.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither page has a real repeatable interaction beyond ordinary cross-document navigation; fabricating a synthetic loop would not represent the site.
checkOutcomes.reason: Neither page has a real repeatable interaction beyond ordinary cross-document navigation; fabricating a synthetic loop would not represent the site.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The heap summary reports 26,459 nodes and 763,644 self-size bytes, a small footprint proportionate to a two-element static page.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap constructor summary and DOM/source inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The single-state heap summary contains no Detached* constructor among its reported populations, and the page ships no scripts, timers, observers, or event-listener registration code.

principleOutcomes.reason: This exposed surface is a bare directory/diagnostic token with no safe user capability or transactional form for an agent to invoke; adding WebMCP tooling would not be meaningful. The surface performs no language, summarisation, classification, or other inference task where a built-in on-device model would improve the experience.

paths.description: Public entry page and directory listing, representing the only index/template exposed by navigation.
Only linked destination, representing the site’s sole visible primary journey and detail/status response.
Unknown-route failure state, selected to test HTTP error recovery.

findings.summary: The public entry page does not explain its purpose or useful next action
findings.evidence: The desktop screenshot contains only “Index of /” and a filename link; there is no AFIP service description or task-oriented CTA.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace directory listing with a real landing/error page that names the service, audience, status, and primary next action.

findings.summary: The only visible journey ends at an opaque, context-free token
findings.evidence: Following a.html produces only “fe010”, with no heading, explanation, next step, or return link.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the destination a semantic document, meaningful status explanation, navigation context, and a clear return or next action.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot remains the same white/black light surface, and no CSS or color-scheme declaration exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven light/dark surface and text colors with a safe fallback.

findings.summary: The only route change is an abrupt cross-document swap
findings.evidence: The link to a.html uses no view-transition CSS and the destination provides no continuity cue.
findings.suggestedFix: After fixing destination semantics, add a subtle cross-document View Transition with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Mobile devices receive a scaled 980px layout instead of responsive reflow
findings.evidence: At 360x800, layout metrics show clientWidth 980, scale 0.367, and hasViewportMeta false on both pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standards meta viewport and use fluid intrinsic layout/text sizing that reflows at the device width.

findings.summary: Document structure is incomplete, especially on a.html
findings.evidence: The homepage exposes no landmarks, and a.html has no title, heading, landmark, or contextual navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic header/main/nav landmarks and give every page a descriptive h1 and logical reading/focus order.

findings.summary: A missing favicon produces a console/network error on every load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse logs a 404 for /favicon.ico and the HAR records the failed request.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an intentional favicon or explicitly reference an existing icon so the page loads without a 404.

findings.summary: The responses use quirks-mode or no authored HTML structure
findings.evidence: The homepage uses an HTML 3.2 doctype and reports BackCompat; a.html is a six-byte text response.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve HTML5 documents with <!doctype html>, UTF-8 metadata, semantic head/body structure, and standards mode.

findings.evidence: The homepage title is “Index of /” with no description; a.html has no title or description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add unique descriptive titles and concise meta descriptions that match each page’s visible purpose.

findings.summary: Crawl and indexing signals are incomplete
findings.evidence: robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return 404; no canonical/hreflang is present, the link text is only a filename, and viewport metadata is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a deliberate robots policy and sitemap if public indexing is intended, add canonicals, descriptive link text, and viewport metadata.

findings.summary: Security headers and first-party cookie attributes are unsafe
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no CSP, HSTS, or nosniff; both cookies lack Secure and HttpOnly and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly where script access is unnecessary, and Lax/Strict where cross-site use is unnecessary; deploy CSP, HSTS, and nosniff.

findings.evidence: No clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or CSP frame-ancestors is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Define restrictive frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options fallback), Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, plus HSTS and an enforcing CSP.

findings.summary: HTTP failures provide no recovery route
findings.evidence: A tested unknown URL returns a generic Apache 404 with no home link, search, retry, contact, or status guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 with a plain link to the safe entry point and concise recovery/status guidance.

findings.evidence: Both rendered documents have an empty html lang value; Lighthouse fails html-has-lang.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an accurate BCP 47 lang value on every HTML document and use dir when content direction requires it.

taskList.title: Replace the exposed directory/token journey with purposeful semantic pages and recovery navigation
Deploy security headers and safe cookie attributes
Move both responses to standards-mode responsive HTML5
Add descriptive metadata and deliberate indexing signals
Respect dark mode and add subtle navigation continuity
Serve a valid favicon without console errors
